grh_a7f51c9768b43b226fd4.title: Rope of Sand
paragraphs: Mike Davis returns to South Africa two years after being tortured by the diamond syndicate, determined to recover a cache of stones he hid in the forbidden desert. Syndicate men Martingale and Vogel use dancer Suzanne Renaud to win Mike's confidence and learn the location, but Suzanne falls in love with him and secretly tries to keep him alive. Mike gives her a map, then discovers it was passed to Vogel and believes she betrayed him. After surviving another attempt on his life, Mike recovers the diamonds. The final confrontation exposes Vogel as a killer and Martingale manipulates events so Vogel dies rather than share the fortune. Martingale then reveals Suzanne surrendered the map only to protect Mike, and Mike leaves Africa with both the diamonds and the woman he nearly misjudged.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Stan Waxman, Norman Field, William Johnstone, Burt Lancaster, and Donald Morrison. The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].

grh_a75d3b8e9aa481a4ca7e.title: Henry 'Box' Brown
paragraphs: Enslaved Richmond laborer Henry Brown resolves to escape after enduring the brutality of slavery and arranges with a white accomplice and Northern abolitionists to ship himself to freedom inside a wooden crate. To create time for the attempt he deliberately injures his hands so he will be excused from work, then is nailed into the box with only a little food, water and air holes. During the 350-mile journey he is repeatedly turned upside down, jolted, dropped and nearly suffocated as the crate travels by wagon, train and steamer. After about twenty-seven hours the box reaches Philadelphia, where abolitionists open it and find Henry alive. He emerges a free man and becomes known as Henry 'Box' Brown.

grh_a79e83ba719ebf8e0f52.title: Here Comes the Bride - Again
paragraphs: Roger Carmichael and his wife Susan brace themselves when Roger's glamorous mother Elaine announces that she has left her latest husband, Walter, and is coming to Los Angeles. Elaine quickly plunges into another round of romance and adventure, while Roger worries that her restless search for novelty will upset the family yet again. By the end, Elaine admits she is tired of maintaining a perpetually youthful image and decides she wants to enjoy her sixties instead of starting over with another man. Walter arrives ready to reconcile, and Elaine turns a farewell celebration into yet another wedding, choosing to marry him again on the spot.
